problem: Existing audio-visual navigation (AVN/SAVN) relies on precomputed room impulse responses, confining agents to a 1 m grid with 4 orientations and giving spatially discontinuous observations. It also assumes the goal sound is continuous, so agents fail once the goal becomes intermittent or silent.
motivation: Realistic sound-emitting targets (a falling person, a ringing phone) are often short-lived or intermittent, and the agent must keep navigating after the sound stops. Continuous, coherent audio-visual streams and fine-grained actions enable reasoning about how the agent's pose changes relative to the goal, but existing goal-inference modules use only the current audio and lose the goal once it goes silent.
key_idea: MAGNet uses a memory-augmented goal descriptor network that fuses binaural audio, previous action and pose with an episodic memory of past goal embeddings, so goal position and category estimates persist and update after the sound stops.
insight: Both episodic memory and self-motion cues help, and they are complementary. In the ablation on clean environments, SR goes from 32.4 (no GDN) to 33.9 (GDN with self-motion only) or 34.3 (GDN with memory only) and 37.7 (full). Better SELD metrics track better navigation. Oracle2 (goal info kept after silence) reaches 75.0 SR vs 41.4 for Oracle1, showing that goal loss after silence is the main bottleneck. Distractors remain a weakness: MAGNet has the highest DSR and only a small gain under distraction.
method: SAVN-CE task/simulator: built on SoundSpaces 2.0 in Matterport3D with continuous audio rendering at 16 kHz and a 0.25 s step. It accumulates residual reverberation from previous steps for temporally coherent audio, with actions of MoveForward 0.25 m, Turn 15° and Stop.

Multimodal observation encoder: ResNet-18 for RGB and for depth, an action embedding, a pose embedding, and a binaural audio CNN over 4 STFT channels (mean magnitude, IPD sin/cos, ILD). The embeddings are concatenated with the goal embedding and stored in a scene memory of N_s=150.

Memory-augmented goal descriptor network (GDN): an MLP fuses audio, previous action and pose into m_t, which is appended to an episodic memory of N_g=128. A causal transformer encoder outputs the goal embedding e^G and an ACCDDOA head (activity-coupled DOA vector plus distance per category).
Context-aware policy network: a transformer encoder over the scene memory and a decoder queried by the current observation give a latent state, which feeds an actor and a critic.

Training: the GDN is trained online with MSE on oracle ACCDDOA labels over complete episodes, using Adam at 1e-3. The policy is trained with DD-PPO in the two-stage SAVi paradigm, with reward +10 for success, a geodesic-distance-change term, and -0.01 per step.

setting.backbone: ResNet-18 encoders + audio CNN + transformer GDN + transformer encoder-decoder policy (trained from scratch, DD-PPO)
setting.training_data: SAVN-CE train split of 0.5M episodes (adapted from SAVi, Matterport3D scenes, 21 goal categories, 102 distractor sounds); up to 240M steps
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D 128x128 (90° FoV) + binaural audio + relative pose (from initial pose) + previous action
setting.action_space: low-level: MoveForward 0.25 m, TurnLeft 15°, TurnRight 15°, Stop
setting.privileged: none at test time (oracle ACCDDOA labels used only for GDN training supervision; the ground-truth goal category is provided to all methods in Distracted Environments)

numbers.eval_set_note: 1,000 test episodes, averaged over 5 runs; Clean Environments (only the goal emits sound)

numbers_note: The task is new and there is no standard benchmark name, so the results are listed under other:SAVN-CE. The ablation variants (Table 3) are on Clean Environments and are not listed separately.
results: On the new SAVN-CE test set, MAGNet reaches 37.7 SR / 32.9 SPL in clean environments, versus 25.6 / 21.2 for the strongest baseline SAVi, which is the 12.1-point SR gain. In distracted environments the gain is small (19.3 vs 18.5 SR) and MAGNet has the highest DSR (7.8). It remains well below Oracle2 (75.0 SR).
limitations: Under distractor sounds the gains are small and the agent is more often drawn to the distractor (highest DSR).
A large gap to the oracle variants remains, so the GDN still loses goal information after silence.
Training is expensive (about 14 days on 4 A800 GPUs), and the task covers only a single static goal in simulation.
